considered.hypothesis: Expanding trade credit and customer prepayments during a year of *falling* revenue cannot be a mechanical consequence of business volume — it is a deliberate decision by suppliers and customers to increase their exposure to a research-intensive firm whose sales are shrinking, which is the strongest possible informed-party endorsement of a pipeline the income statement has not yet vindicated.
considered.reasoning: This is a state-dependence claim rather than another scaling of the counterparty leg, and it is the sharpest available test against the operating-accrual and liability-growth explanations, because in the conditioning sample the mechanical link between activity and operating liabilities runs the wrong way. The weight is nonzero only for shrinking research-intensive firms, so both extreme legs sit inside that stressed population and the sort is not driven by growth, size or issuance.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Counterparty_Support_By_Industry_Intangibility
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), IND_ADJ(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 1), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The same balance-sheet movement means opposite things in different technological environments: in a knowledge-intensive industry, growing operating liabilities are customers prepaying and partners committing to an unverifiable pipeline, while in a commodity industry they are more often stretched payables at a firm conserving cash, so the interaction should be with the industry's intangibility rather than with the individual firm's spending.
considered.reasoning: This replaces threshold tuning on a firm-level gate with a continuous industry-level moderator, which resolves the population question without the coverage and composition shift the critic identified, since every firm retains a weight and none is deleted. The moderator is an environment characteristic recovered from the industry mean, so a positive result cannot be a firm-level R&D-intensity reweighting of the operating-liability effect.

considered.name: Delayed_Market_Funding_After_Withdrawal
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(LAG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 1), 1)), 0), RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Substitution is a response that takes time: when commercial counterparties withdraw funding from a research-intensive firm in one year and the firm goes to the capital markets in the *following* year, management is replacing informed capital with uninformed capital after having seen the informed verdict, which is the clearest evidence that the raise is not demand-driven financing.
considered.reasoning: Using the lagged counterparty contraction as the gate breaks the mechanical dependence the critic identified — the current-year operating-liability change no longer appears in the expression, so the sign cannot be a reweighted flip of the established contemporaneous counterparty effect — and it makes substitution an identifiable sequence rather than a contemporaneous correlation. Both tails are research-intensive firms that lost counterparty support last year, separated by how aggressively they turned to the market this year.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Research_Follows_Counterparty_Validation
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(LAG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 1), 1), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Causation should also run the other way: when commercial counterparties expand their funding, they are signalling demand, and management that responds by raising research intensity is investing against verified demand rather than against its own optimism, while a firm that receives that signal and cuts research is conceding it cannot exploit the opportunity.
considered.reasoning: All sequencing tests in the archive have run investment-then-funding; reversing the order tests whether the value comes from validated funding or from validated *investment response*, which is a genuinely different economic claim and cannot be a third fit of the same contemporaneous operating-liability effect since the counterparty variable is now the lagged conditioner. Both tails are firms that received expanding counterparty support, separated by whether they reinvested.

considered.name: Commercial_Support_Drawdown
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 5)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Commercial financing relationships are sticky, so what matters is how far a research-intensive firm's counterparty funding has fallen below the peak level its own suppliers and customers once extended: a firm sitting at its five-year high of commercial support retains full ecosystem confidence, while one deep below its own peak has suffered a cumulative withdrawal that annual changes can mask if the decline was spread over several years.
considered.reasoning: Distance-from-peak is a cumulative-erosion statistic distinct from the change, level, own-history rank and expansion count already tested, and it captures multi-year withdrawal that one-year differences and rank positions both miss. It also avoids the degenerate mass problems of the earlier own-history construction because the drawdown is a continuous magnitude, zero only for firms currently at their peak.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Customer_Versus_Technology_Capital_Validation
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xad, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xad, 0), COALESCE(xrd, 0)))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 1), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Different intangible assets are validated by different counterparties: customer capital built by advertising is funded by buyers who prepay and distributors who take inventory, while technology capital is funded by suppliers and development partners, and if commercial funding works as an informed verdict it should bite hardest where the intangible asset is a customer relationship the funder personally holds.
considered.reasoning: The moderator is the *composition* of intangible investment — advertising as a share of advertising plus research — which is a bounded characteristic never used in the archive, and it discriminates between the customer-side and supplier-side readings of the counterparty mechanism rather than rescaling either leg. Firms reporting neither form of intangible spending drop out, and the remaining population spans pure advertisers to pure researchers, so the sort tests the economic identity of the informed party.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Market_Funded_Ramp_Awaiting_Ratification
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(LAG(MUL(INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1), 0), RATIO(sstk, at)), 1), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 1), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: The theme's central case is a research ramp paid for by selling shares, and that case is genuinely ambiguous ex ante; the resolution arrives the following year, when commercial counterparties either put their own money behind the newly funded program or decline to, separating productive equity-financed innovation from issuance that was timed rather than needed.
considered.reasoning: The conditioning variable is a joint state never tested in the archive — last year's equity issuance *in a year when research intensity rose* — so the population is precisely the market-financed intangible expanders the task asks us to sort, and the signed counterparty leg then delivers the verdict. This is a new three-part configuration rather than a lag or window adjustment of the existing ramp signal, and it makes the productive-versus-timed distinction operational within a single population.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Shrinking_Intangibles_Confirmed_By_Counterparties
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 1), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: When a firm's recorded intangible base is shrinking through amortisation, write-downs or divestiture, the open question is whether the underlying businesses are still healthy; if suppliers and customers are simultaneously reducing their funding, two independent parties are confirming deterioration, whereas continued commercial support says the accounting decline overstates the economic one.
considered.reasoning: The moderator is intangible-base *contraction*, a state the archive has only ever tested in expansion form (financed buildup, goodwill increases), so this examines the opposite half of the intangible life cycle where accounting value and economic value diverge most. Both tails consist of firms whose intangible base is shrinking, separated by whether the commercial ecosystem corroborates the write-down, which makes the sort a corroboration test rather than an impairment-drift rediscovery.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Counterparty_Coverage_Of_The_Research_Bill
considered.expression: RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1), ADD(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ABS(SUB(revt, cogs))), ABS(DELTA(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: The economically meaningful quantity is what fraction of a firm's research-and-margin funding base was supplied this year by its commercial counterparties: a large positive fraction means suppliers and customers financed a material share of the innovation effort, a large negative fraction means they pulled that financing out of a firm still carrying the research bill.
considered.reasoning: Every counterparty result in the archive comes from a product of a rank moderator and a signed z-score; this states the same economics as a single bounded ratio in minus-one-to-one, a structurally different interaction form whose monotone two-tailed shape is what generated slope-and-alpha agreement in the archive's best ratio constructions. Including gross profit alongside research in the denominator prevents non-innovators from piling up at the bounds, which was the defect of earlier bounded self-funding indices.

critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical rank-difference of two long-published anomalies (R&D/advertising intensity and the Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net-external-financing effect) with no conditioning structure, so any result is a near-certain rediscovery of their additive combination rather than evidence of a funding-source mechanism.

Conditioning the debt-versus-equity issuance mix on R&D intensity is a genuinely interactive and economically motivated idea, but the construction is fragile — it depends on IND_RANK being non-negative (a centered rank would flip the sign for low-R&D firms) and the un-winsorized ZSCORE of (dltis−sstk)/at will let a handful of levered issuers dominate the spread.

In raw (unranked) levels the financing flows are an order of magnitude larger and more volatile than xrd/at, so the signal will be dominated by net payout/external financing and collapses into the known financing and net-payout-yield anomalies while also duplicating proposal 1.

The expression is internally consistent (product of non-negative ranks, negative expected sign) and the financed-acquirer story is coherent, but both legs are individually established negative predictors (asset/intangible growth and gross issuance), so it risks being an amplified rediscovery of stock-financed-acquirer underperformance rather than a new interaction.

GROWTH of sale divided by three-year cumulative R&D is dominated by sales growth (not research productivity) and explodes for near-zero R&D firms with no COALESCE guard, so the signal is effectively issuance × sales growth — a combination whose natural direction (glamour issuers underperforming) contradicts the stated positive sign.

A rank difference between R&D intensity and multi-year share-count growth is simply the sum of two of the best-documented anomalies (R&D-to-assets and net share issuance/Pontiff-Woodgate), and it is also largely redundant with proposal 1 in this same batch.

The switch from a noisy one-year financing *change* to a net-payout *level*, plus bounded within-industry ranks, is a substantive (not merely cosmetic) reworking of the archive's best-alpha channel, though the net-payout/net-external-financing leg is itself a well-documented anomaly and will likely carry much of the load, so the incremental content rests entirely on the R&D-growth conditioning.

This is the archive's `Issuance_Validated_By_Intangible_Payoff` with the same two ingredients, a monotone rank re-encoding, and the expected sign flipped to match the previously observed slope — post-hoc sign reversal of an already-tested expression is not a new hypothesis and offers no independent evidence.

Collateral quality / debt-overhang conditioning is an economically coherent channel absent from the archive and the expression's direction matches the stated negative prior, though the leverage-change leg overlaps the known debt-issuance and asset-growth anomalies, so the test should be judged on whether the interaction adds beyond that main effect.

Stock-financed acquirer underperformance (Loughran–Vijh, Rau–Vermaelen, plus goodwill-growth/asset-growth effects) is a long-published anomaly, so this is a direct rediscovery dressed as an interaction, and it also re-uses the financed-intangible-buildup ingredients already in the archive.

Funding *instability* is a genuinely new second-moment concept for this pair and the sign is internally consistent, but the five-year volatility window will mechanically load on issuance level and on small high-issuance growth firms, so coverage and the incremental contribution over plain issuance intensity must be checked.

This is the archive's `Intangible_Capital_Per_Share_Accumulation` with a monotone rank transform, industry demeaning, and a 1→3 year horizon tweak — a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different construction motivated by the alpha/slope disagreement.

Algebraically the signal is just 1/(1+external issuance / intangible spend), i.e. a monotone rescaling of the gen-0 Knowledge_Capital_Per_External_Dollar idea whose cross-sectional variation is dominated by the well-documented composite issuance anomaly, and with COALESCE(xrd,0) every non-R&D firm collapses to exactly 0, creating a large degenerate mass that will drive the short leg as an "R&D-reporter" dummy rather than a self-funding measure.

The first leg is literally identical to the archive's Debt_Paydown_By_Intangible_Innovators (MA(xrd/sale,3) industry rank) and the second leg is the same net-payout-versus-issuance construct already tested in Payout_Funded_RD_Expansion, so replacing a rank with SIGN is a cosmetic robustness variant of two already-evaluated signals rather than a new mechanism.

Since gross profit is an order of magnitude larger than R&D for most firms, the "burn" leg is essentially negated gross profitability, so the product is largely the known gross-profitability × composite-issuance pair, and there is an internal inconsistency in that the expression's most extreme long leg (highly profitable firms issuing heavily) is described in the hypothesis only as "ordinary growth funding," not as an expected outperformer.

A within-firm time-series-position differencing of innovation intensity against issuance is genuinely distinct from the archive's cross-sectional rank products and from level-based issuance/R&D anomalies, is bounded and monotone with economically interpretable extremes, though the authors should check that COALESCE(xrd,0) constant-zero histories do not make the first TS_RANK degenerate for the many non-R&D firms.

Post-goodwill-impairment drift is an established published anomaly, and because gdwl is a component of intan the signal asserts that *falling* intangibles plus issuance predicts low returns while the archive's Externally_Financed_Intangible_Buildup asserts the opposite sign for *rising* intangibles plus issuance, a tension the proposal labels rather than resolves.

Advertising intensity is a legitimately unexplored conditioning variable here, but the second leg is the standard share-count-growth issuance anomaly and the claim of orthogonality to advertising level is wrong (the rank multiplier deliberately amplifies high-ad firms), while COALESCE(xad,0) leaves most firms tied at zero so the effective test rests on a thin advertiser subsample.

This is essentially the archive's `Internal_Coverage_Gap_Funding_Choice` with a COALESCE and a dividend term bolted on — a plumbing/coverage tweak rather than a new mechanism, and the COALESCE does not "stabilize the extreme legs" as claimed since it merely dumps a large mass of exactly-zero non-reporters into the middle of the sort while the tails remain the same R&D firms, leaving the second leg as the well-known net-external-financing/net-payout anomaly.

The bounded form is monotone in xrd/(sstk+dltis), so it is close to a mechanical blend of two published anomalies (R&D intensity and net issuance/external financing), and the claim of two non-degenerate tails is wrong — every non-R&D firm with any issuance pins to exactly −1, making the short leg "non-innovators that issue debt" (i.e., asset-growth/issuance in disguise) plus a 0/0 dropout for zero-R&D, zero-issuance firms.

A defensible consolidation of the archive's only joint-evidence signal that makes two substantive (not cosmetic) changes — a signed short leg and a persistent three-year cumulation of a lumpy financing flow — though it remains close kin to the known net-debt-issuance anomaly conditioned on R&D intensity, so the incremental content is modest.

The retention leg (Δceq − sstk) is a genuinely new construct here and the signed-z design does put R&D expanders in both tails as claimed, but it is arithmetically close to net income minus total payout, so it will load heavily on profitability (already an FF5 factor) and it perversely penalizes cash-rich repurchasers who are the archetype of internally funded innovators.

Replacing the degenerate 0/1 dividend gate with a smooth three-year payout-commitment rank and the noisy one-year R&D delta with a trend is a coherent, correctly diagnosed fix that keeps both tails populated by distributors, though the mechanism (payout-protecting myopic R&D cuts) is close to established myopic-underinvestment work and the prstkc term imports the repurchase anomaly.

Debt maturity structure is a genuinely untouched and near-orthogonal financing dimension, the sign convention matches the rollover-risk hypothesis, and the signed leg correctly places intangible-heavy firms at both extremes; the main caveat is that dlc/(dlc+dltt) is undefined for zero-debt firms, which silently drops a chunk of exactly the intangible-intensive population the test targets.

This is a denominator swap on the already-tested Maturity_Mismatch_On_Intangible_Assets, and the swap is not innocuous — dlc/at is a leverage-level variable, so the signal ceases to measure maturity *mix* and drifts toward the archive's already-tested intangible-intensity × leverage interaction, making it a cosmetic-yet-mechanism-blurring variant rather than a substantive improvement.

The moderator collapses algebraically to the industry mean R&D intensity — exactly the same moderator as the archived Issuance_Where_Intangibles_Are_Scarce — so the only change is gross issuance → signed net external financing, which leaves the signal close to a nonnegatively reweighted version of the well-known net-external-financing anomaly rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.

The bounded R&D-stock-to-book-equity mismeasurement index is a genuinely different conditioner from the asset-scaled intensities used throughout the archive and the signed net-repurchase leg gives both tails economic identity; the main reservations are that the two legs individually proxy known anomalies (intangible-adjusted value, net share issuance) and that ABS(ceq) makes the index non-monotonic for negative-equity firms.

Conditioning on being an external financier and sorting on R&D-path stability is a defensible reversal of the archive's financing-volatility tests and the expression's sign direction matches the hypothesis, though VOL(xrd/sale) is heavily contaminated by sales volatility and small-firm noise, so the result may end up proxying size/quality rather than financing credibility.

A simple but coherent stock-based interaction not present in the archive, with a correctly signed expression; the main weaknesses are its triviality as a two-characteristic product whose legs (goodwill intensity, leverage) are individually documented return predictors, and the mechanism's ambiguity about whether option-like risk should earn higher or lower returns.

TS_MAX of issuance/at is mechanically dominated by, and highly correlated with, the 5-year mean, sum and volatility of issuance already tested in Sustained_Selffunded_Innovation_Trend and Fragile_External_Funding_Of_Innovation, so this is a temporal-statistic reshuffle within a repeatedly-failed self-funded-innovation family rather than a new mechanism.

This is a one-knob smoothing variant of the archive's `Hidden_Equity_Behind_Repurchases` (identical mismeasurement leg, identical net-repurchase leg merely summed over three years), so it is a cosmetic persistence tweak rather than a new mechanism — and both legs are themselves well-known anomalies (R&D-to-book value proxy × net share issuance).

The two legs are mechanically entangled — RATIO(R&D stock, R&D stock + |ceq|) is high precisely when book equity is small, which for a given asset base implies high lt/at, so multiplying by NEG(lt/at) largely cancels rather than conditions, leaving a signal that is close to a nonlinear low-leverage/high-R&D quality screen rather than a clean test of who owns the hidden asset.

The indicator direction correctly isolates payout cutters and the sign expectation matches the expression, and the payout-*decreasing* state is a genuinely different conditioning sample from the archive's payout-increasing version, though dividend cuts are rare enough that coverage and extreme-leg stability are real risks and the state is partly confounded with the known dividend-cut event effect.

Effectively a re-encoding of the archive's `Brand_Capital_Built_Without_Dilution` (advertising-intensity moderator × net share retirement, since prstkc−sstk over assets is nearly collinear with −growth in csho), which already delivered a strong slope with essentially zero alpha, so the "out-of-sample mechanism test" framing masks a close variant of an already-evaluated and alpha-null signal.

Internally consistent and a genuinely different conditioning structure from the archive's payout-level moderator (here the change in total distributions is the signal within a fixed R&D-intensive population), though the payoff is likely to overlap with the known payout-increase/profitability channel and the change leg will be dominated by lumpy repurchase timing.

The construction is openly reverse-engineered from prior test statistics ("most slope-productive moderator" × "most alpha-productive financing statistic") on the unsupported premise that two independently failing legs fail for complementary reasons, and the 5-year financing-volatility leg is largely a size/illiquidity proxy that also produced the *opposite*-signed alpha when interacted with intangible intensity in the archive.

The informed-versus-arms-length funding mix is a coherent extension of the archive's only two-sided result and is internally consistent, but the gross issuance term is an order of magnitude larger and far more skewed than the year-on-year change in operating liabilities, so the composite risks collapsing into the well-known net-issuance anomaly conditioned on R&D intensity rather than testing the counterparty channel.

The expression matches the stated mechanism and both legs are bounded/signed as claimed, but pairing the archive's highest-t moderator with its highest-alpha financing leg is a statistically motivated recombination whose economic argument (mismeasurement raises the value of informed-party validation) is asserted rather than distinguishing this from the parent signal, and the ABS(ceq) denominator makes the moderator spike for distressed negative-equity firms rather than for genuine research-mismeasured ones.

This is a near-cosmetic rescaling of the archive's Payout_Flexibility_Among_Innovators, and the bounded share is worse behaved than claimed: it is 0/0 undefined for non-distributors and pins to 1.0 for every pure repurchaser regardless of distribution size, so the top leg becomes "R&D-intensive firms that pay no dividends" rather than "flexible distributors," which is not the stated mechanism.

Relative to the archive's Purchased_Intangible_Base_Financing only the moderator's denominator changes (at instead of gdwl+R&D stock) while the financing leg is identical, so this is a variant rather than a new mechanism, and goodwill-intensity times net external financing is largely a repackaging of the documented acquirer-underperformance and net-external-financing anomalies.

Counting net-payout years is a genuinely different functional form from the magnitude-based financing legs already tested, the expression cleanly implements the stated persistence hypothesis, and the bounded 0–5 count plausibly fixes the single-large-raise domination problem that plagued earlier variants.

A single-leg transplant of the archive's best signal from R&D to advertising intensity is close to cosmetic, but it is honestly framed as a discriminating generalization test on a largely disjoint industry population, is internally consistent, and either outcome is informative about whether the mechanism is about informed-party funding or about R&D firms specifically.

The diagnostic motivation (separating a true interaction from an R&D-reweighted operating-liability/accrual main effect) is legitimate, but the double-centered product is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis, since a positive expected sign implies that low-R&D firms with *contracting* counterparty funding earn high returns — a prediction the stated economics explicitly disclaims ("carries no information") — and the change from IND_RANK to IND_ZSCORE on the moderator is otherwise a mechanical variant of an existing archive entry.

This is a denominator swap on the archive's Counterparty_Funded_Innovation (at → sale), and the claimed diagnostic gain is overstated because percent-of-sales scaling is itself a standard accruals normalization, so it neither breaks the accrual interpretation nor constitutes a substantively different signal.

Internally consistent and mechanically coherent (sequencing establishes purpose, mix establishes provenance), but it is a moderator-for-moderator swap between the archive's two highest-t counterparty signals, so it carries real risk of fitting the same underlying Δ-operating-liability effect a third time rather than adding new information.

This is a statistical blend of two archive legs motivated explicitly by diversification of t-stats rather than by a single economic mechanism — payout composition and trade-credit expansion have no common causal story, and averaging a leg with a null slope into one with a null alpha is a cosmetic recombination, not a new hypothesis.

Substituting net external financing for gross issuance in an existing archive expression is a measurement tweak of Counterparty_Versus_Market_Funding_Mix, and the resulting leg is close to the well-documented net-external-financing anomaly interacted with R&D intensity, a configuration the archive has already tested several times.

Moving the gate from 0.03 to 0.10 is threshold tuning on an already-tested expression, and because the indicator discards the continuous intensity weighting that produced the positive result, any sign change will be confounded with a large coverage/composition shift rather than cleanly resolving the population question it claims to settle.

This is the archive's Counterparty_Versus_Market_Funding_Mix with `dltis` deleted from a two-term issuance aggregate — a component-level rescaling of the arms-length leg dressed up as an information-hierarchy claim, and the promised Sharpe gain is a portfolio-efficiency conjecture rather than a new mechanism.

Direct rediscovery of Delayed_Market_Funding_After_Withdrawal with the issuance term narrowed from sstk+dltis to sstk — a one-term deletion aimed at nudging a t-stat of −1.79 over the line, which is exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

This is the arithmetic union of Counterparty_Support_Despite_Revenue_Decline (conditioner unchanged) and the already-flagged equity-only tweak of the funding leg, so it adds no mechanism beyond the two archive components it stacks and risks compounding their coverage and composition instability.
